summary: Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act to exclude from compensable working hours any voluntary time employees spend outside their regular schedule attending or participating in education, training, or similar programs (whether employer-offered or not), as long as they perform no work for the employer during that time and face no adverse action for nonparticipation.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the FLSA solely to redefine what counts as compensable 'hours worked' for education/training activities. It contains no appropriations, authorizations, or changes to federal spending levels.
No provisions alter tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
The legislation addresses wage-and-hour rules for voluntary training and has no connection to health insurance, coverage, or medical care delivery.
No references to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill affects immigration status, visas, border enforcement, or pathways to citizenship.
The text is silent on reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions touch defense budgets, military pay, or national security spending.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation policy.

While the FLSA sets baseline wage rules, this amendment only clarifies non-compensable training time and does not expand or contract eligibility or benefits under welfare, SNAP, Medicaid, or similar programs.

The bill facilitates voluntary worker training by excluding such time from paid hours, but it does not involve K-12 funding, school choice mechanisms, federal education grants, or public-school policy.
No content related to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The legislation contains no sentencing, policing, or criminal-procedure provisions.
Nothing in the bill concerns tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No fiscal measures that would affect deficits or debt reduction strategies.
The bill does not address nondiscrimination protections or legal status for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions on foreign assistance or international aid programs.
The text is unrelated to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No data-privacy, surveillance, or technology-regulation content.

The bill directly amends the FLSA definition of hours worked to exclude voluntary, off-hours education/training programs (with explicit conditions that the activity be non-compulsory and that employers not penalize non-participation). This expands employer flexibility regarding compensable time and interacts with existing collective-bargaining carve-outs for clothes-changing time. The net effect tilts modestly toward employer flexibility rather than new worker or union protections.
No language concerning religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination rules.
